questions.prompt: How should the code be organized for the queue simulation approach to Implement Stack Using Queues?

choices.label: Push into an empty helper queue, then transfer the old active queue behind the new value. Swap queues so pop and top use the active front.
choices.feedback: That matches the selected approach. Push into an empty helper queue, then transfer the old active queue behind the new value. Swap queues so pop and top use the active front.
choices.feedbackCode:
class MyStack:
  operation __init__:
    apply operations or helper calls; update working state
  operation push:
    traverse the required work; apply operations or helper calls; update working state
  operation pop:
    apply operations or helper calls; return the computed result
  operation top:
    return the computed result
  operation empty:
    apply operations or helper calls; return the computed result

choices.label: Append every new value to the active queue's back and pop its front.
choices.feedback: That remains FIFO rather than the required stack order.

choices.label: Copy values into the helper without emptying the active queue.
choices.feedback: The queues must exchange roles cleanly; old contents cannot remain duplicated.

choices.label: Transfer active values before enqueueing the new value into the helper.
choices.feedback: The new value needs to end up at the front to become the next pop.
